quiz_item.question: When examining and storing collectible coins for Coin Collecting Requirement 1, how should you hold a coin to preserve its numismatic grade, and what do the mint marks 'P', 'D', 'S', and 'W' indicate?
options: A. Pinch the flat obverse and reverse faces firmly between bare thumbs and scrub tarnished coins with baking soda paste; the letters indicate purity grades of platinum, diamond, silver, and tungsten.
B. Hold coins with serrated steel pliers and store them loose in PVC vinyl pouches; the letters indicate the four quarters of the fiscal year.

C. Hold a coin only by its outer rim/edge over a soft pad so skin oils do not etch the flat surfaces, and recognize 'P', 'D', 'S', and 'W' as the U.S. Mint facilities in Philadelphia, Denver, San Francisco, and West Point.
D. Polish every coin with steel wool to make it shine before gluing it into a cardboard album; the letters indicate the last initial of the President.

pamphlet_excerpts: Hand-Signed Colonial Note Sheets: Colonial notes were printed in sheets of eight or 16 designs and then numbered and signed by hand, usually by two or three, and sometimes (p. 25).
Founding Fathers' Inked Signatures: Several members of the Continental Congress and others who signed the Declaration of Independence inked their names onto the paper money (p. 25).
Interest-Bearing Redeemable Paper Notes: Many of these notes paid interest and could be exchanged or redeemed for their current value (p. 25).
Punched Circular Redemption Holes: Large circular holes punched into the notes were just one of the ways to show redemption (p. 25).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Redeem Interest-Bearing Colonial Notes: Many of these notes paid interest and could be exchanged or redeemed for their current value (p. 25).
Step 2 - Punch Holes for Cancellation: Large circular holes punched into the notes were just one of the ways to show redemption (p. 25).
Step 3 - Preserve Cancelled Note Curios: These cancelled notes were saved by the states but were released to collectors as curios many years ago (p. 25).
